title: Minimax Risk for Observational Discrete ATE with Surrogate-Assisted Outcome Annotation
banked_reason: Stage 0.5 BELOW NOVELTY FLOOR: tier incremental < floor field; NOT salvageable in scope; paper-score ceiling 5.9 versus field threshold 7.4.
gap_reasons: Stage 0.5 (typed) BELOW NOVELTY FLOOR (triage, round 0) — D0.5.G tier=incremental < floor=field (target=field) and NOT salvageable in scope
proof_attempt_summary: D0 developed a matched signed-residual minimax rate, a same-class converse, and an exact subparametric phase criterion; the theorem graph passed its maximality audit after a signed-bound dependency repair. D0.5 assessed the delivered paper at incremental tier, below the fixed field floor, and stopped before formalization. Two cited statement mismatches and two exposition findings remain; the independent validity check found them repairable but insufficient to raise the novelty tier.
tldr: The causal target is the observational discrete average treatment effect, identified by baseline adjustment; the post-treatment surrogate is never treated as a confounder. For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), the matched minimax squared risk is \(r_{\mathrm{int}}=\min\{1,N^{-1}+\nu n^{-1}+\min\{d,n\}n^{-2}+d^2/(N^2\log^2(en))\}\); exact fair treatment removes the final propensity-learning term. A total signed three-pool estimator attains the upper bound, same-class constructions give the converse, and the resulting subparametric phase conditions are exact.
gap: Surrogate-assisted causal papers derive regular efficiency bounds, while discrete causal minimax papers expose rare-cell and unknown-propensity difficulty. The semisupervised discrete average-treatment-effect annotation frontier retains an \(n^{-1}\) outcome-annotation floor and therefore does not represent the deterministic-quality regime \(\nu=0\), fixed \(d\), and \(N/n^2\to\infty\), where the candidate surface has the smaller \(n^{-2}\) occupancy floor.
fill: The project targets matching upper and lower bounds in \(n,m,d,\nu\), a fully observed-data signed residual estimator, a termwise same-class converse with a separate noisy residual witness and deterministic below-\(1/n\) occupancy and propensity witnesses, and an algebraic corollary giving the exact criterion for when cheap surrogate records yield \(o(1/n)\) risk.
